> From raw reads to a phylogeny — the pipeline, and where it lies to you.

## About this section

Section 2 covered methods that learn from data. This section covers the
computational pipeline that *produces* that data — and the artifacts it
introduces at every step.

The running example is hepatitis B virus, using real sequencing data from
Botswana.

## The modules

| | Module | Core idea |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Sequence Data & Quality Control](1-sequence-qc.qmd) | FASTQ, Phred scores, adapters; what to trim and what to keep |
| 2 | [Mapping & Variant Calling](2-mapping-variants.qmd) | Reads to reference; why coverage and depth are different |
| 3 | [Genotyping & Recombination](3-genotyping.qmd) | Assigning genotype; why recombinants break naive classifiers |
| 4 | [Phylogenetics](4-phylogenetics.qmd) | Building trees; what bootstrap values do and don't mean |

## The through-line

::: {.callout-important}
## Every step is lossy
Extraction favours some templates. PCR duplicates inflate apparent depth.
Basecalling guesses. Alignment forces a read to a position that may be wrong.
Variant calling applies a threshold someone chose.

By the time you have a VCF, five judgement calls stand between you and the
biology. Knowing they happened is the difference between analysis and
credulity.
:::

## Prerequisites

Comfort with the Unix command line. The pipeline tools run outside R.
